articles.heading: Scope & Key Requirements (Public Summary)
articles.text: Sets out overarching requirements for an entity to disclose material information about sustainability-related risks and opportunities useful to primary users of general purpose financial reports, structured around governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics & targets.

articles.heading: Four-Pillar Core Content & Materiality
articles.text:
Built on the TCFD structure, IFRS S1 requires disclosures across FOUR core pillars for all material sustainability-related risks and opportunities:
• Governance (IFRS S1.26–27): governance bodies/individuals overseeing sustainability risks, skills, reporting cadence, and remuneration linkage.
• Strategy (IFRS S1.28–42): short/medium/long-term risks & opportunities, business model and value chain effects, current and anticipated financial effects, and resilience.
• Risk Management (IFRS S1.43–44): processes to identify, assess, prioritise, and monitor sustainability risks and integration with overall enterprise risk management.
• Metrics & Targets (IFRS S1.45–53): cross-industry and industry-specific metrics (referencing SASB Standards under S1.55) and progress against targets.

articles.heading: Financial Materiality, Connected Information & Transition Reliefs
articles.text:
• Investor-focused materiality (IFRS S1.17–19): aligned with IAS 1/IFRS 18 — information is material if omitting, misstating, or obscuring it could reasonably be expected to influence primary users' decisions.
• Connected information & reporting boundary (IFRS S1.20–24): same reporting entity and reporting period as the related financial statements.
• Transition reliefs (IFRS S1.E3–E6): 'climate-first' relief permits reporting only climate-related disclosures (IFRS S2) in the first annual reporting period, plus comparative-period relief.
• China comparison: China's 《企业可持续披露准则——基本准则（试行）》 adopts the same four-pillar structure while incorporating 'double materiality' (impact materiality + financial materiality).

documents.title: IFRS S2 Climate-related Disclosures
documents.version_note: In force from 1 Jan 2024; targeted amendments issued Dec 2025 effective 1 Jan 2027.
documents.summary: Sets out specific climate-related disclosure requirements (physical and transition risks, Scope 1–3 GHG emissions, scenario analysis, and industry-based metrics) designed to be applied together with IFRS S1. Targeted amendments issued Dec 2025 take effect 1 Jan 2027.

articles.heading: Scope & Key Requirements (Public Summary)
articles.text: Sets out specific climate-related disclosure requirements (physical and transition risks, Scope 1–3 GHG emissions, scenario analysis, and industry-based metrics) designed to be applied together with IFRS S1. Targeted amendments issued Dec 2025 take effect 1 Jan 2027.

articles.heading: Climate Risks, GHG Emissions (Scope 1–3) & Scenario Analysis
articles.text:
• Climate-related risks & opportunities (IFRS S2.10–14): distinguish physical risks (acute/chronic) and transition risks (policy, legal, technology, market, reputation); disclose transition plans and capital deployment.
• Climate resilience & scenario analysis (IFRS S2.22): use climate-related scenario analysis commensurate with entity's circumstances.
• Cross-industry climate metrics (IFRS S2.29): absolute gross Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 GHG emissions (measured per GHG Protocol unless jurisdiction requires another method), financed emissions for financial institutions, internal carbon prices, and climate-linked executive remuneration.
• Targeted Amendments (Dec 2025, effective 1 Jan 2027): provide targeted reliefs for certain Scope 3 Category 15 financed emissions (e.g., derivatives, facilitated emissions) and GICS classification.
